blocks.heading: Pick Your Route with the Four Questions

items.text: Run each shortlisted route through the four questions: your fit, your situation, the job market and AI-proofing.
Court days start early, include long waiting and need stamina.
If long waiting and standing drain you, test a desk route before you commit years to chambers.

blocks.heading: Pass Three Proofs Before You Commit

items.text: The four questions says whether a route fits on paper.
Do not lock in an LLM, a coaching fee or a chamber before passing all three proofs.
Do one real task in the route: draft a legal notice, summarise a judgment for a layperson, write a one-page DPDP compliance checklist, or review one contract.
Rule 49 says an advocate cannot be a full-time salaried employee and continue to practise.
Rule 36 bans advertising and solicitation, and the Bar Council warned against social media promotion in March 2025.

blocks.heading: Compare the Practical Paths
blocks.sourceSectionTitle: What each law degree stage unlocks

rows: BA LLB, BBA LLB or BCom LLB (5-year integrated, after Class 12)
A law degree with a second subject built in: humanities (BA), business (BBA) or commerce (BCom).
AIBE, which final-semester students with no backlogs can sit. Then enrolment with a State Bar Council.
3-year LLB (after any bachelor degree)
Law on top of a first degree in anything, so the first degree is your edge.
The AIBE requirement is the same. Entry to the course itself is by each university or college, so check its own notice.
LLB finished, AIBE not yet cleared
A degree and provisional enrolment. You can learn in a chamber or firm, but you cannot yet file or argue on your own.
AIBE XXII is scheduled for 29 November 2026 (tentative). Clearing it gives the Certificate of Practice.
LLB with AIBE cleared
The licence to practise in court as an advocate.
No further licence. Next steps include a chamber seat, a firm interview, a state judicial notice or finding clients.
LLM
A specialisation label and, with UGC NET, a path into teaching and research.
CLAT PG for the National Law Universities. UGC NET Law needs an LLM with 55 percent (50 percent for reserved categories).
BA LLB, BBA LLB or BCom LLB (5-year integrated, after Class 12)

BA LLB suits routes that run on reading, writing and public law: policy, judiciary, teaching. BBA LLB suits contracts, company law and compliance. BCom LLB suits tax, accounts-heavy disputes and company secretary work.
3-year LLB (after any bachelor degree)
Engineering points toward technology and IP work, commerce toward tax and securities, science toward pharma and regulatory work. This is a judgment about where scarce combinations sit, not a rule.
LLB finished, AIBE not yet cleared
Do not leave this to the last month. Every court route, and the judiciary clock, starts after enrolment.
LLB with AIBE cleared
This is where route choice starts to matter, because a full-time salaried job can end your right to appear in court (see the Bar Council section).
LLM
Worth it when it unlocks a named route (teaching, a niche practice). Weak when it only delays a decision.

blocks.heading: Route Map: Ten Routes, Labelled
blocks.sourceSectionTitle: The route map: ten routes, labelled

rows: 1. Privacy, compliance and legal-tech advisory

No exam entry requirement beyond the LLB for most employed roles. If you want to advise outside clients as an advocate, check with your State Bar Council whether your planned work counts as practice. The DPDP Rules were notified on 14 November 2025 and most duties start about 18 months later, so firms have a fixed deadline to prepare for.
Scalable
2. Your own chambers, boutique firm or legal-services business
AIBE and State Bar Council enrolment. Rule 36 limits how you can advertise.
Scalable with a business layer
3. Arbitration and dispute resolution

No fixed qualification to be an arbitrator: parties choose, and the old Eighth Schedule list was removed in 2021. Appearing as counsel needs AIBE. Panels at institutions commonly look for around ten years of experience.
Scalable with a business layer
4. Company secretary and corporate compliance
CSEET, then the ICSI Executive and Professional stages. Graduates from any stream can sit CSEET.
Scalable with a business layer
5. Corporate law firm associate
Campus or interview hiring, with the strongest pipeline from top National Law Universities and a few other colleges. Then AIBE and enrolment.
Not so scalable
6. In-house counsel
Hired by a company, usually after firm or other experience. Under Bar Council Rule 49, a full-time salaried job stops you practising as an advocate in court.
Not so scalable
1. Privacy, compliance and legal-tech advisory
Sell fixed packages: a compliance audit, a policy pack, a staff training session, a monthly retainer.
Mostly one stage: proof of skill. The general compliance level is crowded, so a sector niche matters.
2. Your own chambers, boutique firm or legal-services business
The route is the business: you set fees, add juniors, build repeat and referred clients and own a niche.
Two stages: a chamber or firm seat to learn, then a client base large enough to live on.
3. Arbitration and dispute resolution
Counsel practice first, then appointments as arbitrator, plus drafting and ADR advisory services.
Two stages: years as counsel, then the trust of parties and institutions.
4. Company secretary and corporate compliance
A practising company secretary firm handling filings and governance for small companies.
An exam ladder over several stages, then the work of finding clients.
5. Corporate law firm associate
After years of experience: a boutique firm or independent advisory. Inside the firm, income follows a promotion ladder.
Two stages: getting the seat, then the climb to partner, which few reach.
6. In-house counsel
Later: independent advisory or a boutique practice, if you leave the salary.
Mid-career hiring, then very few top posts such as general counsel.

visuals.alt: Checklist: Own Chambers or a Boutique Firm.
visuals.caption: Questions to use before deciding.
visuals.heading: Own Chambers or a Boutique Firm

items.text: Pick one court or one practice area and become the name for it, instead of taking every brief.
Turn repeat work (notices, agreements, filings, compliance checks) into fixed-fee packages with a written scope, so you quote once and deliver faster each time.
Write down how you do each recurring task as a short checklist.
Take a deposit or part payment on larger engagements, price change requests separately, and keep business money apart from personal money.
Check current GST, tax and registration rules for professional services on the official portals.
Do not depend on one senior, one platform or one client for all your work.

blocks.heading: Bar Council Rules on Advertising and Jobs

items.text: Soliciting work or advertising, directly or indirectly, through circulars, advertisements, touts or interviews not warranted by personal relations.
Sign-boards, name-plates or stationery that claim a specialisation, a past Bar Council post or a judgeship.
Photographs in connection with cases you handled.
Promotional videos, social media campaigns and influencer or celebrity endorsements.

blocks.heading: What AI Changes, Route By Route

items.text: Use AI for first drafts, summaries and a search starting point, then check every citation and clause yourself.
Never paste client documents into a tool without checking how it stores data, because client confidentiality is a professional duty.
Keep a short log of what the tool got wrong.
